NASA and the Department of Energy just signed an agreement to advance space nuclear technologies. What if we powered a permanent Martian base using compact nuclear fission reactors instead of solar panels? Radioisotope power systems and fission reactors provide continuous, high-density energy regardless of dust storms or lack of sunlight, making heavy industrial processing and deep-space travel actually feasible. Would you trust nuclear energy to keep astronauts alive on Mars? Follow for more what-ifs.
